label: Photoshop
blurb: Learn Adobe Photoshop from the workspace to pro texture tricks, built for making art and seamless textures for Horizon.

lessons.title: The Photoshop Workspace
lessons.subtitle: Where your tools live
steps: The Tools bar sits on the left. It holds every tool you click to work with.
The Options Bar runs along the top. It changes to match the tool you pick.
Your image, called the canvas, fills the middle of the screen.
Panels on the right hold Layers, Color, and more. The Window menu lists them all.
Press Tab to hide all panels for a clean view. Press Tab again to bring them back.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Hover over any tool to see its name and its keyboard letter.

quiz.q: Where does the Options Bar appear?

lessons.title: Create A New Document
lessons.subtitle: Start with the right size
steps: Click File then New, or press Ctrl N, to open the New Document box.
Type a Width and Height in pixels. For a texture, try 1024 by 1024.
Set Resolution to 72 for screen and games. Use 300 only for print.
Set Color Mode to RGB. Screens and Horizon both use RGB color.
Set Background Contents to Transparent when you need see-through areas.
Click Create to open your fresh blank canvas.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: For game textures only the pixel size matters, not the DPI number.

quiz.q: Which color mode do screens and Horizon use?

lessons.title: Open And Place Images
lessons.subtitle: Two ways to bring art in
steps: File then Open makes the picture its own new document.
File then Place Embedded drops the picture into your current file as a layer.
A placed image comes in as a Smart Object, so it scales without losing quality.
You can also drag an image file from your folder straight onto the canvas.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Placing keeps your original safe. Press Enter to finish placing it.

right.label: File > Place
right.caption: Drops in as a new layer

quiz.q: What does File then Place Embedded do?
choices: Adds the image as a layer

lessons.title: The Move Tool And Layers
lessons.subtitle: Stacked like clear sheets
steps: Press V to grab the Move tool, then drag to slide a layer around the canvas.
Each layer is like a clear sheet stacked on top of the others.
The top layer covers the ones below it wherever they overlap.
Press Ctrl J to duplicate the selected layer.
Use the arrow keys to nudge a layer one pixel at a time.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Turn on Auto-Select in the Options Bar to click a layer to grab it.

quiz.q: Which key picks the Move tool?

lessons.title: The Layers Panel
lessons.subtitle: Add, hide, and reorder
steps: Click the new layer icon at the bottom of the Layers panel to add a layer.
Click the eye icon to hide a layer. Click it again to show the layer.
Drag a layer up or down in the list to change its stacking order.
Double-click a layer name to rename it. Good names keep you organized.
Select a few layers, then press Ctrl G to group them into a folder.
Lower the Opacity slider at the top to make a layer see-through.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Hold Ctrl and click layers to select many at once, then group them.

quiz.q: What does the eye icon do?

lessons.title: Selection Tools
lessons.subtitle: Choose what to edit
steps: A selection is the marching-ants outline. Your edits only touch inside it.
Press M for the Marquee to draw boxes and circles.
Press L for the Lasso to draw a free shape by hand.
Press W for Quick Selection, then paint over what you want to grab.
The Magic Wand, also under W, picks areas of one similar color.
Press Ctrl D to deselect when you are done.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Hold Shift to add to a selection. Hold Alt to subtract from it.

quiz.q: Which key deselects everything?

lessons.title: The Brush Tool
lessons.subtitle: Paint with color
steps: Press B to pick the Brush tool, then drag on the canvas to paint.
Press the [ key to make the brush smaller. Press ] to make it bigger.
A hard brush has sharp edges. A soft brush fades out at the sides.
The brush paints with your foreground color. Change it in the Color panel.
Hold Alt and click to grab a color from the image, then keep painting.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Set brush Hardness in the Options Bar, or press Shift [ for softer.

quiz.q: Which key makes the brush bigger?

lessons.title: The Eraser Tool
lessons.subtitle: Erase with care
steps: Press E to pick the Eraser, then drag to rub pixels away.
On a normal layer the eraser leaves clear, see-through pixels.
On a locked Background layer it fills with the background color instead.
The eraser deletes for good. Later you will learn masks, which are safer.
Set the eraser size with [ and ], just like the brush.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Double-click the Background layer to unlock it so erasing goes clear.

quiz.q: On a normal layer, erasing leaves what?

lessons.title: Fill And Paint Bucket
lessons.subtitle: Flood an area fast
steps: The Paint Bucket, under G, fills an area with your foreground color in one click.
Press Alt Backspace to fill the whole layer with the foreground color.
Press Shift F5 to open the Fill dialog with more choices.
A bucket fill spreads until it hits an edge of a different color.
Select an area first to keep the fill inside that shape.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Press D to reset your colors to black and white before you fill.

quiz.q: What does the Paint Bucket do?

lessons.title: Color And The Eyedropper
lessons.subtitle: Pick and swap colors
steps: Two swatches sit near the bottom of the Tools bar: foreground and background.
Click the top swatch to open the Color Picker and choose any color.
Press X to swap the foreground and background colors.
Press D to reset them to the default black and white.
Press I for the Eyedropper to sample a color straight from your image.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: While using the Brush, hold Alt to borrow the Eyedropper for a second.

quiz.q: Which key swaps the foreground and background colors?

lessons.title: Transform And Flip
lessons.subtitle: Resize and turn layers
steps: Press Ctrl T for Free Transform. A box with handles wraps your layer.
Drag a corner handle to resize. It keeps the proportions for you.
Hold Shift while dragging a corner to stretch it freely instead.
Hold Alt to resize from the center outward.
Right-click inside the box to find Flip Horizontal and Flip Vertical.
Press Enter to apply, or press Esc to cancel.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: In newer Photoshop, corner drags keep shape by default. Shift unlocks it.

quiz.q: Which keys start Free Transform?

lessons.title: Crop And Canvas Size
lessons.subtitle: Trim or add room
steps: Press C for the Crop tool. Drag the edges to cut away the parts you do not want.
Press Enter to apply the crop. The trimmed pixels are removed.
Image then Canvas Size does the opposite: it adds blank space around the art.
Canvas Size uses an anchor grid to choose which side the new space goes.
Image then Image Size changes the pixel size of the whole picture.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Uncheck Delete Cropped Pixels to keep the hidden edges for later.

quiz.q: What does Canvas Size do?

lessons.title: Text For Thumbnails
lessons.subtitle: Big bold words
steps: Press T for the Type tool, then click once on the canvas to start typing.
Pick a font and size in the Options Bar. Bold, thick fonts read best.
Set the text color with the color swatch in the Options Bar.
Press Enter on the number pad, or click the check mark, to finish the text.
Use the Move tool, V, to drag the text where you want it.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Add a stroke or shadow in Layer Styles so text pops off any background.

quiz.q: Which key picks the Type tool?

lessons.title: Adjustment Layers
lessons.subtitle: Fix color without damage
steps: Click the half-filled circle at the bottom of the Layers panel to add one.
Brightness/Contrast makes the image lighter, darker, or punchier.
Hue/Saturation shifts colors and makes them richer or more gray.
Levels controls the darks, mids, and lights for a better range.
Adjustment layers sit on top and never touch the real pixels below.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Each adjustment layer has a built-in mask so you can limit where it works.

quiz.q: Why use an adjustment layer?
choices: It does not harm the pixels

lessons.title: Layer Masks
lessons.subtitle: Hide without deleting
steps: Click the mask icon, a rectangle with a circle, at the bottom of the Layers panel.
A mask is a hidden sheet: white shows the layer, black hides it.
Paint with black on the mask to hide parts. Paint white to bring them back.
Gray paint makes parts only partly see-through.
Masks beat the eraser because nothing is ever truly deleted.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Press X to swap black and white while painting a mask to fix mistakes.

quiz.q: On a mask, black paint does what?

lessons.title: Blend Modes
lessons.subtitle: How layers mix
steps: Blend modes decide how a layer mixes with the ones under it.
Find the dropdown at the top of the Layers panel. It starts on Normal.
Multiply darkens the image and drops out white. Great for shadows.
Screen lightens the image and drops out black. Great for glows and light.
Overlay boosts contrast, darkening the darks and lightening the lights.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Hover the mouse over a blend mode name to preview it live on your art.

quiz.q: Which blend mode lightens and drops out black?

lessons.title: Seamless Tileable Textures
lessons.subtitle: Tiles with no seams
steps: A seamless texture repeats across a surface with no visible edges or lines.
Open Filter then Other then Offset, and turn on Wrap Around.
Set the offset to half the width and half the height. The old edges move inward.
Now the seams sit in the center where you can clearly see them.
Use the Spot Healing Brush or Clone Stamp to paint over and hide the seams.
Save at a power-of-two size like 1024 so it tiles cleanly in Horizon.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Keep lighting flat and even, or the repeat will show obvious bright spots.

quiz.q: Which filter helps make a texture seamless?

lessons.title: Export As PNG
lessons.subtitle: Save art for Horizon
steps: Click File then Export then Export As to open the export window.
Choose PNG as the format. PNG keeps transparency, which Horizon needs.
Make sure Transparency is checked so your clear areas, the alpha, stay clear.
Set the size to a power of two like 512 or 1024 pixels.
Click Export, pick a folder, and save the file.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Save As also offers PNG. Keep a layered PSD copy so you can edit later.

quiz.q: Why export as PNG for Horizon?

lessons.title: Texture Resolution
lessons.subtitle: Power-of-two sizes
steps: Game engines love power-of-two sizes: 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 pixels.
These sizes load fast and show cleanly on the headset.
For most Horizon textures, 1024 by 1024 is a good top size.
Bigger is not always better. Large textures eat memory and slow the world.
Match the texture size to how big the object actually looks in the world.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: A small prop rarely needs over 512. Save the big sizes for hero art.

quiz.q: Which is a power-of-two texture size?

lessons.title: Non-Destructive Workflow
lessons.subtitle: Keep every edit undoable
steps: Non-destructive means you can always go back and change an edit later.
Convert a layer to a Smart Object to scale and filter it without quality loss.
Use adjustment layers for color instead of editing the pixels directly.
Use masks to hide parts instead of the eraser to delete them.
Keep your layers separate and save a master PSD before you flatten or export.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Smart Filters live on Smart Objects, so you can re-edit a blur any time.

quiz.q: What makes a workflow non-destructive?
